title: Farewells
label: ch:farewells
canDo: I can end a German conversation politely, choose a farewell that fits the situation, and write German's three distinctive marks — the eszett, the umlaut, and a capital on every noun.

payoff.summary: German parts formally with a promise to see each other again, casually with a word that travelled from French through Walloon and Low German before it got here, and softly with bis — "until" — plus a word for time. This chapter takes auf Wiedersehen apart into the three words it is made of, then teaches bis as a recipe and fills its slot three times: bald, später, morgen. GE-C04-practice closes the arc with the first conversation that runs from hello to goodbye.
payoff.note: Chapter 4 is now generated from schema-v2 lessons, so the payoff is atom-scored rather than authored. It claims all thirteen lexical atoms — the three words auf Wiedersehen is built from, the two register-bearing goodbyes, and the bis recipe with each of its three time words — plus the four transferable grammar rules the chapter teaches: that a capital separates der Morgen from morgen, that the eszett marks a long vowel, that an umlaut marks a grammatical change, and Grossschreibung itself. The writing atoms belong here because chapter 4 owns the three writing lessons as well as the farewells; leaving them out put the payoff at 14/30, below the 0.5 representativeness floor. The per-word pronunciation and etymology atoms are drilled in their own lessons and are deliberately not claimed.
